Article Title: Instagram gets first logo update in 10 years, internet jokes it now reads 'Instagzam'
Article Text:
Instagram's new logo

Instagram head Adam Mosseri says it was time for a refresh

Internet quickly pokes fun at new Instagram logo

Meta-owned photo sharing platform Instagram has rolled out its first logo update in a decade. But the redesign is already drawing mixed reactions online. While Meta says the new wordmark is "cleaner and more modern," many users have joked that the updated lettering makes the app's name difficult to read. Some said it looks like "Instagzam," while others compared it to "Instagwam" and even questioned whether the new design meets accessibility standards. The app's familiar multicoloured camera icon remains unchanged, with only the wordmark at the top of the app getting a new look.Announcing the redesign, Instagram head Adam Mosseri said the company wanted to modernise the logo after keeping it unchanged for 10 years.“The wordmark at the top of the app hasn't changed in 10 years, so it was time for a refresh,” Mosseri wrote in an Instagram post. He added, “Cleaner and more modern, with references to the original and the simplicity and craft that's always made it Instagram.”Mosseri also shared the announcement on Threads, writing, "Thought I'd share this on Threads [too] and see what the hot takes might be."The redesigned wordmark quickly became a talking point on Instagram and X (formerly Twitter), with many users saying some of the letters are difficult to recognise.One user commented, "Is it just me or It reads : instagzam ❓."Another wrote, "Instagwam – how a toddler would pronounce it. Perfect."Others joked that the logo looked like "Instaguam," while another user said, "It's barely readable. Does it even pass accessibility checks? Booo. I might be the outspoken minority, but do not like."While the logo attracted plenty of attention, some users said Instagram should focus on other issues affecting the platform. "Adam, while Instagram gets a new look, thousands of legitimate creators and businesses are losing their accounts without clear explanations or real support," said one user responding to Mosseri’s post.
Article Summary: Instagram has rolled out its first logo update in a decade. Many users have joked that the updated lettering makes the app's name difficult to read. The app's familiar multicoloured camera icon remains unchanged, with only the wordmark at the top of the app getting a new look.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: 360-degree CCTV camera equipped police vans to nine police stations from Aug 15
Article Text:
Nashik:





The city police will deploy nine state-of-the-art ‘Mobile-1’ squad vehicles from Aug 15 to respond to serious crimes and monitor crowded and sensitive locations. The vehicles, already in the city, are equipped with 360-degree CCTV cameras, floodlights and up to 1 TB of onboard data storage.The vehicles also have an elevated seating area that functions as a mobile ‘watch tower’, making them particularly useful during the upcoming Simhastha Kumbh Mela.On the orders of police commissioner Sandeep Karnik, the nine vehicles will initially be allotted to nine of the city’s 14 key police stations. The remaining stations will receive vehicles in a subsequent phase. Police officers and personnel are currently being trained to operate the system.At present, when police receive a call, a Beat Marshal reaches the spot first, assesses the situation and seeks additional support if required. The Mobile-1 squad will now be deployed in such serious cases.Each vehicle can accommodate eight to 10 personnel and has an internal ladder leading to the upper deck. The elevated platform will allow police to monitor crowds and security situations from the vehicle, reducing the need to erect separate watch towers during major deployments.The Mobile-1 vehicles are fitted with CCTV cameras and floodlights on all sides, enabling night-time video recording and live filming of incident sites. The system will also facilitate monitoring of crowds during marches, riots, protests and other law-and-order situations.The city police currently operate several mobile units, including Peter Mobile, the mobile squad of a senior PI; CR Mobile, the patrol squad within a police station’s jurisdiction; DB Mobile of the crime detection branch; Beat Marshals on two-wheelers; Dial 112 for emergency response; and Damini Marshals for women’s safety.The new Mobile-1 squads are expected to strengthen the police’s response and surveillance capabilities, particularly during the Simhastha Kumbh Mela.
Article Summary: The vehicles, already in the city, are equipped with 360-degree CCTV cameras, floodlights and up to 1 TB of onboard data storage. Each vehicle can accommodate eight to 10 personnel and has an internal ladder leading to the upper deck. The elevated platform will allow police to monitor crowds and security situations from the vehicle.

Article Title: IIT Madras launches musical fountain, exclusive gym for female students within the campus
Article Text:
IIT Madras launches musical fountain, exclusive gym for girl students within the campus

Chennai:





IIT Madras on Saturday launched an exclusive gym for female students, a musical fountain on campus and an exclusive space for outside-classroom activities as part of its student wellness initiatives.IIT Madras director V Kamakoti launched these facilities after Independence Day celebrations on the campus. Gajendra Circle, one of the important landmarks within the IIT campus, will feature a music and lights show along with the water fountain every evening from 7pm to 7.15pm.“It is scientifically proven that listening to music and watching the flow of the water significantly lowers the cortisol levels, reduces anxiety and refreshes the brain. It will help students, faculty members and other residents to relax and recharge themselves amid their demanding schedules,” said professor Sathyanarayana N Gummadi, dean of students, IIT Madras.A gym for female students is another key initiative for making the campus inclusive for women.“About 30% of the 10,000 students housed at IIT Madras are girl students. Earlier, they were given exclusive access from 3pm to 5pm.During this time, girl students were attending classes and labs. So, the institute has come up with an exclusive gym for them,” Gummadi said.The institute also earmarked a space for outside-the-classroom activities at Nalanda Square near the Students Activity Centre.“The open-air space hosted interactive, non-classroom learning activities such as life-skill courses and outbound training (OBT) for all freshers to emphasise the importance of teamwork. Any faculty member at IIT Madras who wants to take classes in an open-air environment or encourage outdoor activities can bring their students to this square,” he added.Earlier, the institute also launched other initiatives such as a protein mess for sportspersons and an inclusive centre in the library to help students with disabilities to access resources with assistive devices.
Article Summary: IIT Madras director V Kamakoti launched these facilities after Independence Day celebrations. Gajendra Circle, one of the important landmarks within the IIT campus, will feature a music and lights show along with the water fountain every evening from 7pm to 7.15pm.

Article Title: ‘Robot boys’ steal show at Kavundampalayam govt School’s Independence Day event
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Students dressed up like robots stole the show at Independence Day celebrations at Kavundampalayam Government Higher Secondary School on Saturday.The school marked the 80th Independence Day with a blend of patriotism and technology as students from its STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) laboratory took part in the parade and flag-hoisting dressed up as “robot boys. ”The robot-themed presentation drew attention for its creative use of innovation and STEM concepts, earning appreciation from those present. Trainers from the iExplore Foundation guided and supported the students in executing the idea.The school launched the “Cyber Champions Ambassador Programme” to promote cyber safety, responsible digital behaviour and effective use of technology. Under the initiative, selected student leaders will be trained to spread awareness on digital safety, cyber hygiene and online threats and to mentor peers.The celebrations highlighted the school’s focus on STEM education, creativity and digital awareness, with coordinated efforts from the administration, teachers, iExplore Foundation trainers and students.
Article Summary: Students from Kavundampalayam Government Higher Secondary School dressed up as “robot boys’ ” The robot-themed presentation drew attention for its creative use of innovation and STEM concepts. The celebrations highlighted the school’s focus on STEM education, creativity and digital awareness.

Article Title: Ferrari’s first all-electric car sells for $40 million at charity auction, nearly 40 times initial estimate of $1.1 million; buyer won’t receive it until 2027
Article Text:
Ferrari’s Luce “Chassis 0” sets a new auction record after selling for $40 million at charity auction.

Ferrari Luce breaks previous $26 million record

Ferrari Luce packs four electric motors, 1,050 cv of power, a 310 km/h top speed and a 530 km claimed range.

What makes the $40 million Ferrari Luce special?

With a 122 kWh battery, 800V architecture and 1,050 cv, Ferrari’s Luce accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in just 2.5 seconds.

Ferrari Luce packs more than 1,000 horsepower

Ferrari’s Luce brings supercar performance to its first EV.

Ferrari aims to make its EV feel like a Ferrari

Ferrari’s first all-electric vehicle has made history even before reaching its buyer. A bespoke 2026 Ferrari Luce, identified as “Chassis 0” and described as the first production chassis from the Luce programme, sold for exactly $40 million at an RM Sotheby’s charity auction in Monterey on Saturday.As Road & Track reported, the record-breaking sale makes the electric Ferrari the most expensive new car ever sold at auction. The auction house waived its buyer’s premium, meaning the entire $40 million will go to The Ferrari Foundation, which plans to use the proceeds for future educational initiatives.Despite the eye-watering sale price, the buyer will not take delivery of the car until the first quarter of 2027. The vehicle is expected to return to Ferrari’s headquarters in Maranello before being delivered.The $40 million sale surpassed the previous record set in 2025, when a customised Ferrari Daytona SP3 sold for $26 million at auction.The Luce’s result is particularly notable given the criticism Ferrari faced from some traditionalists following the unveiling of its first fully electric model. Ferrari introduced the Luce in May with a starting price of €550,000, or around $636,356.The vehicle represents a major departure from Ferrari’s traditional combustion-engine sports cars. The model was designed in collaboration with LoveFrom, the design studio founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive.The auction car was created through Ferrari’s Tailor Made programme and was designed around the theme of light. Its bespoke exterior is finished in Madreperla Semi-Gloss, featuring a dedicated pigment that shifts between green and violet depending on the angle and intensity of the light.Inside, the cabin is upholstered in Perla Le Mans metallic leather made from selected Swiss hides. Other interior elements that would typically be black have been finished in Grigio Corvara.The car also features bespoke wheels, customised brake calipers and a Ferrari logo set against an optical-white background. Ferrari says the complexity of the paint application means that no two examples will look exactly alike.However, the biggest distinction is its “Chassis 0” status. Ferrari describes it as the first production chassis of the Luce programme, giving the buyer a unique piece of the marque’s electric-car history.According to Ferrari’s official website, the Luce is powered by four electric motors, with one motor driving each wheel. The powertrain produces 1,050 cv and allows the car to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 2.5 seconds.The electric four-door has a claimed top speed of 310 km/h and a range of 530 kilometres on a full charge. It uses a 122 kWh battery pack, an 800-volt electrical architecture and weighs 2,260 kilograms.Ferrari describes the Luce as a spacious hatchback capable of seating five people.The vehicle uses a new vehicle control unit designed to network its various systems, with targets updated 200 times per second. The front motors produce 210 kW at the axle, while the rear motors generate 620 kW.Ferrari has also focused heavily on preserving the driving character associated with its combustion-engine models.The Luce features a separate elastically mounted subframe, which Ferrari says is a first for the brand and helps reduce unwanted vibrations. A precision accelerometer at the centre of the rear axle monitors the natural frequencies of rotating components.Ferrari says those frequencies are then processed to create a sound reminiscent of the brand’s traditional engines, using an approach similar to that of an electric guitar.The car also features a Torque Shift Engagement system designed to progressively deliver torque during cornering. An e-manettino manages power, torque curves, traction and performance through Range, Tour and Performance settings.Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna said after the car’s unveiling that the Luce had attracted orders from both existing and new customers.“The Ferrari Luce has nothing to do with electric cars you have seen from other players,” Vigna said in May, adding that customers would need to see and drive the car to understand how distinct its design, performance and interior are.With its $40 million charity-auction sale, the Ferrari Luce has now secured a place in automotive history before its first customer delivery.
Article Summary: A bespoke 2026 Ferrari Luce sold for exactly $40 million at an RM Sotheby’s charity auction in Monterey on Saturday. The sale makes the electric Ferrari the most expensive new car ever sold at auction. Despite the eye-watering sale price, the buyer will not take delivery of the car until the first quarter of 2027.

Article Title: 'I don’t feel rooted here': Indian couple in Ireland to return to Pune after 11 years, citing AI pressure and job stress
Article Text:
NRI couple in Ireland for 11 years to move back to Pune and raise daughters with grandparents.

Spent 11 years in Ireland

'I don't feel rooted here'

Internet reacts

An Indian tech couple living in Ireland for more than a decade say they plan to move back to Pune by May next year, citing rising work pressure, concerns about artificial intelligence and the lack of family support while raising their two daughters.The couple shared their plans in a Reddit post, saying their children currently spend most of their day in childcare and school-related arrangements because the family has no relatives nearby.They said their routine in Ireland typically runs from 8am to 6pm, with the children moving between creche, breakfast club, school and after-school care while both parents work.“In Pune they walk out of school into their grandparents' home. This single picture does more work in my decision than any spreadsheet,” they wrote.The couple said returning to Pune would mean their daughters could spend more time with their grandparents, while the family would also have help with cooking and household chores.After 11 years in Ireland, the couple said they no longer wanted to manage work, childcare and household responsibilities without family support.They also said they were increasingly worried about the pressure created by technological and AI changes in the workplace.The couple argued that their parents' ability to spend time with their grandchildren is more valuable now than waiting another decade.“The grandparents' healthy years are now. Not in 10 years, when we'd return for hospital duty instead of daily life,” they wrote.They said their parents had previously visited Ireland for a month but found the experience difficult, making a permanent move there unrealistic.The couple also described a sense of detachment after spending more than a decade in Ireland.They said they had built a functional life there but still did not feel they had developed deep roots.“After 11 years I don't feel rooted here myself,” they said.They also described missing the everyday family and cultural connections they associate with India, arguing that celebrations and social life felt different when experienced away from their wider family.The couple said they had generally found Ireland more welcoming than the UK or US, but still felt that subtle experiences of being an outsider could affect children growing up there.Several users responded with their own experiences of living in Ireland.One user said they had moved to Ireland only recently with an infant but were already considering returning to India.“I'm in Ireland as well; I moved here recently(not even months) and am still feeling that I should move back to India. We moved here with our infant thinking it'll be better for her future, but considering the health and the daily hustle here, it feels like India would be better. She can decide for herself whether she wants to move back here or not, but we definitely are moving back within a year.”Another user said changing attitudes towards immigration could also influence people's decisions to remain in Ireland or Britain.“I would add one more reason to do so: Ireland and Britain are on a trajectory of becoming less and less welcoming to immigration. Ireland and especially the Britain that is now is not what it will be in 5 years.”A third user responded:“Wish you all the best! Good decision.”
Article Summary: Indian tech couple living in Ireland for more than a decade say they plan to move back to Pune. They cite rising work pressure, concerns about artificial intelligence and the lack of family support while raising their two daughters. The couple said returning to India would mean their daughters could spend more time with their grandparents.

Article Title: Minnesota teen Evan Morris built a low-cost system that detected seizure-like activity in worms and triggered ultrasound; recurrence fell 70.1% in his model
Article Text:
Evan Morris (Image Credit: Society For Science)

How the system works

Seizure recurrence fell

Why the research matters

Eighteen-year-old Evan Morris of Saint Paul, Minnesota, has developed a low-cost experimental system that could offer researchers a faster way to study how brain stimulation might control seizures. His project, called SILENCE: On-demand seizure suppression via closed-loop sonogenetics, uses genetically modified worms, a computer-controlled detection system and ultrasound to identify and interrupt seizure-like activity. According to the Society for Science, which presents the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) awards, Morris received the $10,000 Mary Sue Coleman Award for Life Science Innovation & Impact in 2026 for the project. In his experiments, the system reduced seizure recurrence by 70.1% and lowered overall seizure activity by nearly 30%.The project is based on a concept called sonogenetics, an approach that uses ultrasound to influence genetically modified cells. Morris worked with Caenorhabditis elegans, a tiny worm widely used in biological research because its nervous system can be studied in controlled laboratory experiments.To make the worms responsive to ultrasound, Morris used gene editing to introduce an ultrasound-sensitive channel into their brain cells, according to the Society for Science. He then developed a computer-controlled system capable of identifying seizure-like activity in the worms. When the system detected the abnormal activity, it automatically activated an ultrasound stimulus designed to interrupt it.This creates what is known as a closed-loop system. Instead of applying stimulation at predetermined intervals, the system continuously monitors activity and responds when it detects a specific event. That distinction is important for studying neuromodulation. Researchers investigating brain stimulation need to determine which stimulation parameters, such as timing and intensity, produce the most useful effects. Finding those settings can involve repeated experiments and considerable trial and error.Morris's system was designed to make that process faster and less expensive by allowing stimulation to be automatically delivered when seizure-like activity occurs.The results were particularly notable because the system did more than simply detect abnormal activity. Morris used it to test different stimulation settings and determine which ones were most effective at suppressing seizure-like behaviour.According to the Society for Science, the experiments showed a 70.1% reduction in seizure recurrence, while overall seizure activity fell by nearly 30%. The results are notable because they show that the system could be used to test different stimulation settings in a living model.Morris's work does not mean that the worm system is itself a treatment for epilepsy. Instead, its potential lies in providing researchers with an experimental platform for studying how stimulation affects neural activity and for identifying promising settings before moving toward more complex studies.One of the most interesting aspects of Morris's project is its combination of biology, engineering and computer control. The system brings together genetic modification, ultrasound stimulation and automated seizure detection rather than relying on a single laboratory technique.The low-cost design could also make repeated experiments more accessible. If researchers can rapidly test many stimulation parameters in a living model, they may be able to identify promising approaches more efficiently. As per the Society for Science, Morris's work could contribute to faster, lower-cost ways of studying brain stimulation in living systems. The project also earned Morris first place in the Cellular and Molecular Biology category at the 2026 Regeneron ISEF.The broader significance is therefore not that a teenager has developed a ready-made epilepsy treatment, but that he has created a relatively inexpensive experimental system for exploring a difficult problem in neuroscience. By allowing seizure-like activity to be detected and stimulation to be delivered automatically, Morris's work demonstrates how closed-loop technology could help researchers investigate more precise approaches to controlling abnormal brain activity.His results provide an early proof of concept in a worm model, and further research would be needed to determine whether similar approaches can eventually translate to more complex biological systems and, ultimately, human medicine.
Article Summary: Evan Morris of Saint Paul, Minnesota, has developed a low-cost experimental system that could offer researchers a faster way to study how brain stimulation might control seizures. His project, called SILENCE: On-demand seizure suppression via closed-loop sonogenetics, uses genetically modified worms, a computer-controlled detection system and ultrasound to identify and interrupt seizure-like activity. In his experiments, the system reduced seizure recurrence by 70.1% and lowered overall seizure activity by nearly 30%.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card

Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Before the knowledge walks out the door
Article Text:
Everyone in Silicon Valley is racing to build machines that replace human expertise.

Ahmer Inam

, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it.

When Ahmer Inam appeared on Fox & Friends in June, his mother watched the segment without following much of it. Her English is limited. There was her son on the famous curved couch of American morning television, fielding questions about artificial intelligence, and she understood almost none of the words. She wept anyway. Some distances need no translation, and the one between a schoolteacher's household in Delhi and a Manhattan television studio is legible in any language.Had she followed the argument, it might have surprised her less than it surprised the audience. Because what Inam was defending, underneath the vocabulary of frontier AI, is approximately the oldest idea in civilisation — the one his father practised for a living: that knowledge survives only when one generation troubles to hand it to the next.Inam has spent twenty-five years building artificial intelligence — long enough to remember when it meant symbolic logic in the late nineties, and senior enough to have run AI and data for Fortune 500 companies, Nike and Wells Fargo among them, back when "chief AI officer" was still an exotic title. He is not, in other words, a critic sniping from the cheap seats. Which makes the thesis of Cognisee, the research lab he founded and leads, sound almost seditious in today's Silicon Valley: "We're not trying to replace the worker," he says."We're trying to make the worker irreplaceable."The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage." By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030 — electricians, welders, machinists, the hands America needs if it is serious about building factories, chip plants and grid capacity again. But Inam's diagnosis is sharper than a headcount. "America does not have a work shortage," he likes to say. "It has an expertise shortage."Consider what actually leaves the building when a master electrician retires at sixty-eight. Not the manual — the manual stays. What leaves is the ear that catches a motor running slightly wrong two weeks before it fails; the instinct that connects a faint vibration to a pattern in old maintenance logs; forty years of judgment that was never written down because it could not be. The philosopher Michael Polanyi had a name for this — tacit knowledge, the things we know but cannot tell — and Cognisee is, at bottom, a bet that the most valuable training data on earth is tacit.The company's method has a fable-like symmetry. Its AI begins as an apprentice: it works alongside experienced people and learns what they notice, what they ask, how they make judgment calls. Then it turns around and becomes a coach, carrying that accumulated judgment to the newcomer. "First it's an apprentice," Inam says. "Then it becomes a coach." Picture a 22-year-old on his first aircraft-maintenance job, hearing a sound he has never heard before, with the distilled instincts of the country's best technicians beside him in real time. "He's not being replaced by a machine," Inam says. "He's being mentored by one."The repository where all this lives is called, a little grandly, a Wisdom Vault — a secure library of hard-won know-how from doctors, nurses, electricians, factory workers, farmers, small-business owners. Grand or not, the name gives away the emotional register Inam is working in. This is not pitched as workforce optimisation. It is pitched as inheritance.He is careful — insistent, actually — about the question that framing invites: who owns it? In Cognisee's design, the expert decides what to preserve, what to share, and with whom; the contributor is recognised and rewarded; the knowledge belongs to the person who earned it, not to the machine that absorbed it. "There is a big difference," Inam says, "between being monitored and being mentored." The company is incorporated as a public benefit corporation, which he describes as a legal commitment to the worker rather than a marketing pledge.That ownership principle is also where his quarrel with the reigning AI paradigm becomes explicit. The frontier labs, Inam argues, got intelligent by swallowing the written internet — and the written internet is now substantially swallowed, which is why the industry's plan increasingly amounts to bigger data centres and more electricity, even as some of the field's own pioneers warn of a wall ahead. His contrarian wager is that the next leap will come not from more compute but from the knowledge that never made it onto the internet in the first place — and that it can be gathered by consent rather than by crawler.For an Indian reader, the resonance is hard to miss. This is a country that has watched its weaves, its remedies and its craft knowledge catalogued, carried off and sold back to it before. It is also a country whose deepest teaching traditions were never textual at all, but moved from person to person — the guru-shishya parampara, the ustad and the shagird. Inam has spoken about Wisdom Vaults for indigenous and medicinal knowledge, with communities retaining ownership of what they contribute. One way to describe Cognisee is as an attempt to give the world's oral inheritances an infrastructure layer — sovereignty included.The idea is attracting converts from unexpected quarters. Cognisee's co-founder, Alex Giannou, spent nearly two decades on Wall Street financing precisely the data centres and power deals behind the AI boom; he crossed over, in Inam's telling, because the right bet and the smart bet turned out to be the same one. Among the company's early backers is a senior Google executive who helped invent federated learning, one of the foundational privacy-preserving techniques of modern machine learning. And last year the XPRIZE Foundation, where Inam serves as a Visionary, recognised his work with its Global Visioneering Award.None of which quite explains the conviction. For that you have to go back to Delhi. Inam grew up in a low-income household, the son of a teacher — a man who spent his working life on the least scalable expertise-transfer technology ever devised: one adult, one room, one generation at a time. The son's journey to America was not gilded; there were stretches, early on, when he could not always afford to eat. It takes a particular kind of person to emerge from that and conclude that a nation's most undervalued asset sits not in its server farms but in the heads of its retiring machinists and nurses."Every generation should start where the last one left off," Inam says. It sounds like a product principle. It is closer to a family creed — the thing his father practised without ever calling it a thesis, the thing his mother recognised on a television screen in a language she does not speak. Some knowledge, it turns out, transfers just fine.
Article Summary: Ahmer Inam, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it. The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage" By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of…”
Article Text:
Image: AP News

Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos

“I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.”

What does this quote mean?

Limitations can force us to think differently

Necessity has a long history of creating innovation

Frugality can make innovation more efficient

Constraints can turn problems into creative challenges

Creativity often grows outside the comfort zone

Why this quote still matters today

Innovation is often associated with having more, more money, more resources, more advanced technology and more time. But some of the most creative solutions emerge when those advantages are limited. Jeff Bezos captured this idea when he said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress. Sometimes, they force people to think differently, question familiar methods and find solutions that would never have emerged in more comfortable circumstances.Jeff Bezos (1964-present) is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He built the company from an online bookseller into one of the world's largest technology and e-commerce businesses and has also pursued ventures in space exploration through Blue Origin.This statement implies that scarcity of resources can be an impetus for innovation. When there are no simple solutions, people are obliged to rethink how to do things.Tight budget, shortage of materials, or technical difficulties can become the grounds for experimenting rather than excuses for inaction. The main message that Bezos tries to convey here is that constraints can make people innovative.In the case of abundance of resources, it is easy to find a solution by adding more resources, people, tools or funds. Constraints take away that luxury. All of a sudden, efficiency becomes the priority, and common assumptions should be questioned. A constrained team might discover a simpler way of doing things just because they do not have enough means to operate according to the traditional way.Useful innovations have often been developed due to people’s needs for solving certain problems using what was already available at hand. In cases ranging from simple farming implements to sophisticated medical gadgets that operate in conditions of limited resources, necessity has proved time and again to breed creativity. In the absence of an apparent solution, people start to search for other ways of solving their problems.Innovation does not necessarily mean that you should develop something that is larger or more complicated than your current product. Some of the most outstanding solutions come when people try to do the same thing using less material resources or reducing superfluous steps in a process. This way, frugality may become another incentive for inventors to find what really matters.It may seem as if a hard constraint makes the issue a roadblock. However, perceiving a limitation as a challenge will make a difference in the mindset when it comes to dealing with an issue. The question from “Why can't we do this?” will turn into “How could we do this differently?” This approach can foster experimenting and coming up with unique ideas.Comfort can help one to carry on with the things as usual. Constraints break up the sense of comfort. They make one think and come up with new options. Regardless of whether one is starting a business, developing a product or even solving a simple problem, constraints can provide a different perspective of creativity than abundance can.Whether it be startups trying to innovate on meager resources or scientists innovating the technology to suit a harsh environment, innovations often emerge when there is a sense of urgency involved. The words of Jeff Bezos provide an excellent point that lack of resources should not necessarily translate into lack of opportunities. In some cases, the very fact that there is no easy way out leads to innovation of a solution. The lesson from the statement is quite straightforward: Innovation occurs when nothing else works.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress.

Article Title: Can I use soapy water to clean TV screen? Here’s what you should know
Article Text:
Tips to to clean TV screen safely (AI-generated image)

How to clean TV screen safely with soap

Dip a clean microfiber cloth into the solution

Wring it out thoroughly so it is only slightly damp.

Wipe the screen gently using light, circular motions without pressing hard.

Once clean, use a dry microfiber cloth to remove any remaining moisture.

Things that you should never use to clean your TV screen

Never use glass cleaner on a TV screen

Avoid paper towels

Don't use household cleaning sprays

Skip rubbing alcohol and harsh chemicals

Never spray water directly on the screen

Don't use rough cloths or old rags

Avoid excessive pressure while cleaning

Avoid baby wipes or wet wipes

Don't use abrasive sponges or scrubbers

Cleaning a TV screen looks like a simple job, but the wrong product or tool can scratch the display, strip its protective coating, or cause permanent damage. Modern LED, OLED, QLED and Mini-LED televisions come with delicate anti-glare and anti-reflective coatings that need careful handling. One question often asked is whether one can use soapy water to clean a TV screen? The short answer is: not directly. While a small amount of diluted soapy water may be recommended for stubborn stains, using too much soap, spraying liquid directly on the display, can damage the screen's protective coating or allow moisture to seep inside the TV.If you need to remove stubborn fingerprints or greasy marks, use only a very small amount of mild dish soap mixed with distilled water.Note: Avoid using strong detergents or excess soap, as they can damage the screen's protective coating.Experts say only approved cleaning methods should be used, and have flagged several household items that people commonly reach for by mistake. Here's a look at what to avoid when cleaning your TV screen, and why.Most glass cleaners contain ammonia, alcohol or other harsh chemicals that can damage the protective coating on modern displays.These products may work fine on windows or mirrors, but on a TV screen they can leave streaks and permanently alter its finish.Paper towels may feel soft, but they contain wood fibres that can scratch the screen over time. Addiitnally, they can also leave lint behind, making the display look dirtier after cleaning.Multi-purpose cleaners, kitchen cleaners and disinfectant sprays are not designed for electronics. Spraying them directly on the TV can damage its screen and may allow liquid to seep into the edges of the screen.Strong cleaning agents such as rubbing alcohol, acetone, bleach or ammonia-based products can strip away the anti-reflective coating found on many modern televisions. Once damaged, the coating cannot be restored.Water sprayed onto a display can run down and seep into the TV through its edges or vents, raising the risk of internal damage. If moisture is needed, a lightly dampened microfiber cloth is the safer route.Old T-shirts, towels, tissues and rough fabric can carry dirt or coarse fibres that scratch the display. A clean microfiber cloth remains the safest choice for wiping away dust and fingerprints.Pressing hard on the screen can damage the display panel, especially on OLED and LED TVs. Use light, gentle strokes instead of scrubbing stubborn marks.Wet wipes or for that matter baby wipes contain cleaning chemicals, fragrances or moisturisers that are not safe for TV screens. Using wet wipes on screen can leave residue and may damage the coating over time.Kitchen sponges, scouring pads or abrasive cleaning tools can permanently scratch the TV screen, even with gentle use. These products should never be used on electronic displays.
Article Summary: Cleaning a TV screen looks like a simple job, but the wrong product or tool can scratch the display, strip its protective coating, or cause permanent damage. Experts say only approved cleaning methods should be used, and have flagged several household items that people commonly reach for by mistake.

Article Title: Apple threat notifications: What is mercenary spyware and how to protect against it
Article Text:
What exactly is Apple's threat notification

What to do if you get Apple threat notification

General security tips for everyone

Apple recently sent notifications to customers who it suspected to have been targeted with spyware in their devices. The tech giant later confirmed to multiple publications that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. By sending these alerts, the company reminded users about one of the most sophisticated digital threats currently in existence: mercenary spyware. If you are one of those who got the term “Apple threat notification” flashing on your screen and wondered what it actually means, here's a breakdown of what these alerts are, why they are sent and what you should do if you ever receive one.Apple threat notifications exist for one specific purpose: to warn and assist users who may have been individually targeted by spyware attacks. In this case, it was a notification for mercenary spyware. These operations are far more advanced than regular cybercrime, and attackers behind them pour in exceptional resources to go after a very small, specific group of people and their devices.Apple says that these attacks cost millions of dollars to carry out and often don’t stay active for very long, which actually makes them harder to detect and stop in time.The good news, though, is that the majority of users will never come across this kind of attack in their lifetime.Citing public reporting and research conducted by civil society groups, cybersecurity researchers, and journalists over the years, Apple says that this level of individually targeted, high-cost cyberattacks has typically been linked to state actors, including private firms that build mercenary spyware for governments, such as the NSO Group's well-known Pegasus tool. While only a small number of individuals end up being targeted, usually journalists, activists, politicians, and diplomats, these attacks are happening constantly and across the globe.If you ever receive one of these alerts, Apple provides extra guidance and recommends steps you can take to secure your accounts and devices, including turning on Lockdown Mode. The company also strongly recommends reaching out to expert organisations for help, such as the Digital Security Helpline run by the nonprofit Access Now, which offers round-the-clock emergency security assistance.While most people will never encounter mercenary spyware, it's still worth following some basic cybersecurity habits.The first is to keep your devices updated with the latest software so you're covered by the newest security patches, and protect them with a passcode, Face ID, or Touch ID.The second most important thing to do is to turn on two-factor authentication along with a strong password for your Apple Account, and enable Stolen Device Protection for extra peace of mind.While Apple doesn’t allow installing apps from third-party stores, ensure that you download apps only from the App Store, use strong and unique passwords across your accounts, opt for passkeys wherever they're availableFinally, Avoid clicking on links or opening attachments sent by unknown senders.
Article Summary: Apple recently sent notifications to customers who it suspected to have been targeted with spyware in their devices. The tech giant confirmed to multiple publications that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. By sending these alerts, the company reminded users about one of the most sophisticated digital threats currently in existence: mercenary spyware.

Article Title: Fireflies.ai brings its AI notetaker to the inbox with Email Assistant, now free on all plans
Article Text:
Meeting context is the part rival AI email tools can't copy

Fireflies.ai, the AI meeting assistant used by more than 20 million people and teams at 75% of Fortune 500 companies, has moved into the inbox. On Friday the company launched Email Assistant, which plugs into Gmail or Outlook and treats email the way it already treats calls—sorting what lands, labelling it by priority, and dropping drafted replies into the thread before you get to them.The pitch rests on a familiar arithmetic. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index found the average worker receives 117 emails a day, with 40% of people online at 6am already checking mail and nearly a third back at it by 10pm—the "infinite workday" Microsoft has been warning about. Fireflies' argument is simpler than most: if it sat in on the call, it already knows what the reply should say.That is the actual differentiator here. When a prospect or candidate follows up on something discussed weeks ago, Email Assistant pulls from both the thread and past meetings with that person, so users aren't reconstructing the conversation from memory. Auto Labels triages incoming mail without touching existing rules or filters. Auto Draft Replies writes in a tone set through custom Writing Instructions, and nothing sends without review. If a sent email goes quiet, a follow-up is drafted in the same thread after a waiting period you configure. AskFred handles plain-English requests—find an email, summarise a thread, pull this week's action items.Insights from email now also feed the Daily Brief alongside meetings and Slack. Meeting Prep, Tasks and AI Skills will draw on email context in the coming months.Email Assistant is available today across all plans, including the free tier. Pro starts at Rs 955 per seat per month, billed annually. Fireflies says it does not train its models on customer data.
Article Summary: Fireflies.ai's Email Assistant plugs into Gmail or Outlook and treats email the way it already treats calls. It pulls from both the thread and past meetings with that person, so users aren't reconstructing the conversation from memory. Email Assistant is available today across all plans, including the free tier.

Article Title: OpenAI's 612-megawatt facility, ranked among the world's biggest AI data centres, abandons plan to cool servers with recycled water as ...
Article Text:
OpenAI's first ChatGPT-powered device is said to be a smart speaker

What made OpenAI walkaway from recycled water plan

OpenAI has abandoned plans to cool its planned S7 data center in Sydney, Australia, with recycled water. OpenAI nixed the plans in favor of a closed-loop liquid cooling system. According to a report in Reuters, Developers of a massive data centre OpenAI wants to build in Australia have abandoned plans to cool it with recycled water, switching to a more ​energy-intensive method that undercuts government efforts to curb the booming sector's drain on resources.The 612-megawatt 'S7' facility, planned as one of the largest data hubs in the world, initially aimed to tap Sydney’s treated wastewater to chill its servers, which would have reduced dependence on potable water sources and significantly lowered the cooling system's energy requirements. The move was designed to avoid depleting local drinking supplies while minimizing electricity use, according to planning documents filed in April.However, after failing to secure planning permission to build a pipeline to serve the data center, NextDC, the developer, decided to change its plans. Australian data centre operator NEXTDC told Reuters that it walked away from negotiations with local utilities after hitting regulatory roadblocks over the permits needed to construct a dedicated wastewater pipeline. In December 2025, OpenAI and NextDC announced that they had signed a Memorandum of Understanding that would see the ChatGPT-maker use some of the data center’s capacity, with the option to scale over time."Recycled water ... has real merit and it can support lower PUE and better overall sustainability and NEXTDC considers it wherever that infrastructure exists," CEO Craig Scroggie said in an email. PUE, or ​power usage effectiveness, is a closely watched metric of energy used for cooling and other overheads beyond computing. "Potential sources were canvassed in early planning. In Western Sydney, the enabling infrastructure . .. is not yet in ​place," Scroggie is said to have added.The S7 datacentre facility will now rely on a closed-loop liquid cooling system that circulates coolant directly across processing chips and dissipates heat into the air using fans. While the revised system uses no drinking water, analysts say the fan arrays will consume significantly more electricity at a time when Sydney's grid operator warns transmission capacity is already stretched thin by data centre demand.As per launch release S7 datacenter is expected to deliver thousands of direct and indirect jobs over the course of its construction, as well as ongoing technical, manufacturing, engineering and operational roles.
Article Summary: OpenAI abandons plans to cool data center in Australia with recycled water. Instead, it will rely on a closed-loop liquid cooling system that circulates coolant directly across processing chips and dissipates heat into the air using fans. The move was designed to avoid depleting local drinking supplies while minimizing electricity use, according to planning documents.

Article Title: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath to startup founders: Stop saying 'we use AI'; 'Bragging that your product uses AI is like …’
Article Text:
Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath

Nithin Kamath says AI is now 'table stakes'

'Opening your pitch with AI' may hurt startup founders

Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath has shared a post with a message for startup founders trying to impress investors with AI. In a post on X, Nithin Kamath said he has become tired of seeing investment pitch decks that begin by highlighting AI, arguing that using AI is no longer a unique selling point. According to Kamath, AI has become so common that leading a presentation with "we use AI" is more likely to turn investors away than attract them. He said that “bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day”.Sharing his views, Kamath said the number of startup presentations that begin by talking about AI has become excessive. "The number of investment decks I get leading with 'we use AI' is ridiculous. It's reached a point where it automatically makes my eyes roll, and I've almost stopped looking at them," Kamath wrote.He said founders should understand that AI is no longer a competitive advantage by itself. "Founders need to realize that AI is just table stakes now. Bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day. It's not a differentiator."According to Kamath, simply saying a product uses AI does not explain why customers or investors should care.In the post, Nithin Kamath warned that making AI the first thing investors hear could have the opposite effect. "In fact, opening your pitch with it is a surefire way to get ignored, not just by us, but by most serious VCs," he said.Kamath also pointed to another trend created by generative AI. He said AI tools have made it easier than ever for founders to create polished-looking presentations, but that has also made many startup pitches look and sound alike."Especially now that AI has democratized the ability to generate 'nice-looking' decks, the last thing you want to do is say the exact same generic things as every other founder using the exact same tools," he wrote.
Article Summary: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath says AI is no longer a unique selling point. Leading a presentation with "we use AI" is more likely to turn investors away than attract them. Kamath: Bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day.
